title: U.S. Senate · Minnesota

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Sen. Tina Smith (D) announced she would not seek re-election in 2026. In the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary, Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan defeated U.S. Rep. Angie Craig 58.9%-39.5%. In the Republican primary, Michele Tafoya, a former NBC/ESPN sportscaster, defeated Adam Schwarze, Royce White and six others with 51.8% of the vote.

candidates.name: Peggy Flanagan
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over U.S. Rep. Angie Craig, 58.9%-39.5%.

summary.text: Peggy Flanagan is the Democratic (DFL) nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat and has been Minnesota's lieutenant governor since 2019. A citizen of the White Earth Nation, she began as a community organizer, served on the Minneapolis school board and in the Minnesota House, and was elected lieutenant governor on the ticket with Tim Walz. She won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over U.S. Rep. Angie Craig, 58.9% to 39.5%.

background.text: Born September 22, 1979, in St. Louis Park, Minnesota, where she was raised by her mother; she is a citizen of the White Earth Nation and a graduate of St. Louis Park High School. She has described growing up in a single-parent household that at times relied on public assistance.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Minnesota in 2002, in child psychology with a minor in American Indian studies.

Early in her career worked on U.S. Sen. Paul Wellstone's campaign, as an organizer in the urban Native American community, and for the Minnesota Council of Churches; later worked for Wellstone Action, a nonprofit that trained activists, was executive director of the Minnesota branch of the Children's Defense Fund, and was a partner at The Management Center, an executive coaching firm.

Won her first election in 2004 to the Minneapolis Public Schools board and served 2005-2009; she was appointed to the board again in 2010. She briefly challenged a state House incumbent in the 2008 Democratic primary but dropped out.

Elected to the Minnesota House of Representatives (District 46A) in a November 2015 special election, serving until January 2019. In the House she served on the Health and Human Services Reform Committee and co-founded the House Native American Caucus in 2017.

Elected lieutenant governor in 2018 as Tim Walz's running mate, and re-elected with him in 2022; she is the first woman of color elected to statewide office in Minnesota, according to Wikipedia. Her work in the office has included child care, housing and family-assistance programs, and she chairs the Minnesota Interagency Council on Homelessness.
Spoke at the 2016 Democratic National Convention, was one of four chairs of the 2024 Democratic National Convention, and in 2023 was elected chair of the Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association.
Announced her Senate candidacy on February 13, 2025, after Sen. Tina Smith said she would not seek re-election; she won the DFL endorsement on May 30, 2026, and the August 11 primary.

priorities.text: Ending corruption: getting corporate and dark money out of politics, reversing Citizens United, banning stock trading by members of Congress and the president, and banning elected officials from lobbying.
Healthcare: opposes cuts to Medicaid, supports Medicare for All, and says healthcare is a human right.
Affordability: a $17 federal minimum wage tied to inflation, national paid family and medical leave, universal childcare, and expanding the Child Tax Credit.
Housing: supports the Homes Act, down-payment assistance, and banning large corporate landlords and hedge funds from buying single-family homes.
Immigration: says ICE is 'out of control,' supports dismantling the agency and reimagining an immigration system rooted in due process, while also supporting a secure border.

positions.summary: Supports passing the Women's Health Protection Act to restore Roe v. Wade-era protections nationwide, helped Minnesota pass a law protecting abortion access and providers after Roe was overturned, and supports repealing the Hyde Amendment.
Supports banning assault weapons, high-capacity magazines and ghost guns.

Supports dismantling ICE as currently structured, ending what she calls indiscriminate mass-deportation sweeps, and creating a pathway to legal status for long-settled undocumented residents, while also saying the border should be secure.
Supports 'bold action to build more housing,' including the Homes Act, alongside banning corporate/hedge-fund purchases of single-family homes.
Supports expanding the Social Security payroll-tax income cap so wealthier earners contribute more, and says small businesses should not pay a higher effective tax rate than large corporations.
Supports Medicare for All and says healthcare is a human right; opposes cuts to Medicaid.

Opposes the Trump administration's rollback of clean-energy investments and supports wind, solar and other clean-energy development, citing Minnesota's commitment to 100% carbon-free electricity by 2040.
Supports funding local police departments so they have resources to train officers and support community safety, alongside investment in re-entry and recidivism-reduction programs.
Supports a $17 federal minimum wage tied to inflation; co-chaired Minnesota's 2014 Raise the Wage campaign.
Supports universal childcare, saying investment in high-quality programs helps kids and family budgets.

record.text: As Lieutenant Governor, co-chaired the 2014 campaign to raise Minnesota's minimum wage and index it to inflation, and helped lead the effort to pass Minnesota's paid family and medical leave program.
Helped lead passage of the Minnesota Protect Reproductive Options Act, which protects access to contraception, abortion care, family planning and related reproductive healthcare services.

As Lieutenant Governor, oversaw state investments in veterans' programs, including the opening of three new veteran homes and functionally ending veteran homelessness in eight of Minnesota's nine regions.

candidates.name: Michele Tafoya
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary over Adam Schwarze, Royce White and six others with 51.8% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: Former NBC and ESPN sports broadcaster

summary.text: Michele Tafoya is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. A former sports broadcaster, she spent nearly three decades on radio and television, most prominently as an NFL sideline reporter for NBC, and is a first-time candidate. She won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 51.8% of the vote.

background.text: Born December 17, 1964, in Manhattan Beach, California, and attended high school there and in Redondo Beach.
Earned a bachelor's degree in mass communications from the University of California, Berkeley (1988) and an MBA from the University of Southern California (1991).
Began her broadcasting career on Minneapolis radio and television stations, including KFAN radio and WCCO-TV from 1994, and joined CBS Sports in 1994 as a reporter and host.

Worked for ABC Sports and ESPN from 2000 to 2011, including as Monday Night Football sideline reporter, then was sideline reporter for NBC's Sunday Night Football from 2011 to 2022, ending with Super Bowl LVI.
According to her campaign website, she covered 327 NFL games, won four Sports Emmy Awards and two Gracie Awards, and retired from NBC the day after Super Bowl LVI.
Also worked in talk radio, hosting an afternoon show on WCCO radio (2009-2012) and co-hosting the KQRS morning show (2016-2020).
After leaving NBC in 2022 she co-chaired Kendall Qualls's Republican campaign for governor, and later started a political podcast (now The Michele Tafoya Podcast).
Announced her Senate candidacy on January 21, 2026. She and her husband, Mark Vandersall, live in Edina, Minnesota, according to Wikipedia.

priorities.text: 'Stop the fraud': tougher penalties for fraud, including mandatory minimum sentences and deportation of noncitizens convicted of fraud, and stripping federal funding from states that don't implement anti-fraud audit controls.

Law and order: more funding, equipment and training for police; tougher penalties for violent crime; enforcing immigration law and deporting people in the country illegally who are convicted of crimes.
Cutting costs and taxes: opposing middle-class tax increases, cutting prescription drug costs, and supporting an 'all of the above' energy policy.
Keeping transgender athletes out of women's sports, education reform focused on parental rights and test scores, and stronger election-security measures.

positions.summary: Supports enforcing immigration law, deporting noncitizens convicted of crimes including fraud, and cosponsoring a 'Deporting Fraudsters Act'; opposes efforts to abolish ICE.
Says she will push for more funding, equipment and training for law enforcement and opposes efforts to remove legal protections police rely on.

candidates.researchNotes: Tafoya has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and has held no prior elected office, so there is no official voting or legislative record. Positions here are drawn from her campaign website; some issue keys (e.g. abortion, guns, tax_wealthy, tariffs) are not addressed with enough specificity on her site to document a direct stance.

candidates.name: Rebecca Whiting

summary.text: Rebecca Whiting is the Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate. An Army veteran who served as a combat medic, she describes herself as a homeschooling mother and farmer in northern Minnesota. She also ran for this seat in 2024, when she received 1.7% of the vote.

background.text: Born in Picayune, Mississippi; earned a high school diploma from Picayune High School and a bachelor's degree from American Military University in 2010.
Served in the U.S. Army from 2004 to 2007; in a 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said she was a combat medic in Iraq in 2004-05 and 2006-07.
Her career experience includes work as a farmer, baker and small business owner, and she describes herself as a homeschooling mother who raises a large family on a small farm in northern Minnesota.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate in 2024, finishing third with 55,215 votes (1.7%) behind Amy Klobuchar and Royce White.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, or other detailed public statements were found within the research budget for this race.

candidates.name: Marisa Simonetti

summary.text: Marisa Simonetti is an unaffiliated candidate for U.S. Senate. She works in real estate and describes herself as a mother, businesswoman and community volunteer who entered politics after volunteering in her son's school. She is running on housing affordability, public safety and community-focused policies.

background.text: Born in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Minnesota in 2024; she describes it as a bachelor's degree in psychology.
Her career experience includes working in real estate; her campaign materials describe a background in real estate and entrepreneurship.
Says she got involved in politics after volunteering in her son's kindergarten classroom, and that she volunteers in the school lunchroom.

priorities.text: Affordable housing and public safety: says she wants to tackle Minnesota's housing affordability crisis while investing in community-based approaches to reducing crime.
Reducing wasteful government spending and supporting small businesses.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to tackling Minnesota's housing affordability crisis, drawing on a background in real estate.

candidates.researchNotes: Based only on her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses; no independent campaign website was found.
